newsitem.title: GERMANY: Veba, RWE, C&W create new force in German telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Veba, RWE, C&W create new force in German telecoms.

text.p: Germany's two largest utilities, RWE AG and Veba AG, and British-based Cable and Wireless said on Wednesday they will join forces in Germany, creating a powerful challenger to telecommunications monopoly Deutsche Telekom.

The combined networks of RWE and Veba cover thousands of miles along their vast stretch of power lines and will give the new company access to virtually every major city in Germany, in many cases reaching deep into residential neighbourhoods.

It will also for the first time create a telecommunications operator in competition to Deutsche Telekom that can offer a broad range of services from fixed-network telephone services to mobile communications and cable television from one source.
"Our partnership with Cable and Wireless on the German market is strengthened by the alliance with RWE," said Veba Chairman Ulrich Hartmann.

In one of the most far-reaching alliances to emerge on the German telecommunications market, RWE and the Vebacom joint venture owned by Veba and C&W will merge their entire German communications networks into a new company called Netco.
RWE, the larger of the two utilities, will hold a majority of 51 percent in Netco, which will provide network services and infrastructure.

A second company, called Servco, will take charge of product development, provision of service and customer management. Vebacom, in which C&W holds 45 percent, will control 51 percent of Servco. Veba AG will also take a 25 percent stake in RWE's RWECOM unit.
Vebacom and RWE will control the two companies through a joint management company, which will be located in Duesseldorf.

Vebacom will bring its stake in the E-Plus mobile phone group and its cable television activities in Servco, while RWE will bring its activities including RWE Systemhaus. RWE and Veba will merge their entire communications networks in Netco.
The deal values Vebacom at 4.2 billion Gmern marks ($2.7 billion).
